content:
Hello Lean community,

I’m an independent researcher looking to get a large Lean 4 artifact in front of people equipped to inspect it. The project is a proposed proof of Erdős Problem 887, with an unusual workflow: the proof was developed first as a Lean-facing theorem architecture, and then a 123-page manuscript was written backward from that structure into mathematical prose. Because of this, it reads less like a standard number-theory paper and more like a Lean-code/math-paper mirror pair.

The Lean formalization is roughly 14k lines, compiles, and contains no sorry and no non-standard axioms. The manuscript mirrors the theorem-source structure exactly.

Traditional publication routes have deadlocked. arXiv declined the manuscript, requesting conventional journal publication first. Conversely, a journal editor explicitly told me that the length and the Lean-assisted nature of the work made it unsuitable for them, and advised me to put it on arXiv.

I am not asking this channel to evaluate the full number-theory claim on the spot. I am asking what the right Lean-side inspection path is for an artifact of this size and format.

Links:

Manuscript DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20651083
Lean formalization DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20586442
GitHub repository: https://github.com/jarekkoch-hub/erdos887-lean
Theorem/package map: https://github.com/jarekkoch-hub/erdos887-lean/blob/main/Lean_Audit.tsv

Caution on AI inspection: While I encourage the use of LLMs to assist in reading the code, please be aware that current models do not have the reading bandwidth to hold the full tier structure of this formalization simultaneously. This limitation can cause them to produce confident but incorrect readings of the global logic. Please use the provided audit map to help anchor your readings.

With traditional peer review unable to process the format, where and how should a Lean-checked result of this magnitude be presented to the field?

Have you seen this?

https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/887.lean

It might help to modify your proof so that it proves the conjecture as stated in the above Lean file.
if you're able to do that, I think it would help persuade others that you've actually proven the conjecture (as opposed to proving something else)

The proof does not prove Erdos problem 887. It assumes a hypothesis that amounts to saying "assume that we have a function which takes any alleged counterexamples and proves 0 =1. then there are no counterexamples" and then concludes Erdos problem 887.
Fwiw I asked Claude (Opus 4.8) to look at it --> "as it stands the formalization does not verify the four-divisor bound". Will DM you the session so you can review.

Update: I revised the theorem surface to address the confusion around the final wrapper.

The external reconstruction wrapper is now accompanied by an explicit Lean audit identity showing that it is exactly the pair of its two component source packages. It is not a hidden “no counterexamples” assumption. This lean proof uses multiple versions of nested packaging logic, which is why the audit file exists.

Following Matt Diamond’s comment, I also added a Formal Conjectures / DeepMind-facing mirror layer. The divisor-window count, the eventual bound with answer 4, the K = 4 bound, the fully derived Rosenfeld lower construction, and the audit package collecting those outputs are now all stated and proved directly in the Lean file.

To be clear: the formalization was already compiling and blue-checked. These additions are not a replacement for the proof. They are audit-surface hardening so that the theorem architecture is harder to misread from the final wrapper alone.

I also want to re-emphasize my earlier caution about AI sweepers. Both recent AI readings localized on the final wrapper and missed the package structure around it. These tools can help search, but they should not be treated as global proof readers for a file with this much dependency nesting unless the inspection is very carefully scoped.

I will push the updated code and archive materials by the end of the day.
